name: Catering and event food

problems.words: Client says 500 guests, 650 show up, and we run out; headcount changes the night before
quick_ideas: Set a clear cut-off date for the final headcount and tell the client in writing, so late changes have a known rule
Agree up front how extra guests are charged, because it's much harder to discuss on the night.

workzap_build.text: a headcount change log per event with automatic cut-off reminders to the client, linked to the purchase list.

problems.ask_first: When does the client usually confirm the final count?
problems.free_stops: The cut-off and extra-guest terms and how buying adjusts to changes are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the final promised guest count with actual plates served at the next event, so shortage patterns stop feeling random.
Give one person the job of writing every headcount change in one notebook, so kitchen prep uses the latest number.

problems.words: I quote per head but never know if the event actually made money
quick_ideas: Add up the real cost of your last event (food, staff, transport, crockery hire), so you see the true margin once
Compare it with the quote, because the gap shows which cost you're under-pricing.

workzap_build.text: an event costing sheet that totals purchases, staff, transport and crockery against the quoted price for every event automatically.

problems.ask_first: Which costs are hardest to pin down per event?
problems.free_stops: The costing structure and per-head pricing logic go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the quoted menu beside what was actually bought and paid after one event, so the weak items stand out.
Give one person one notebook page per event for all spending notes, so profit checking no longer waits for memory.

problems.words: Bookings tracked on WhatsApp — two events on the same night got confirmed
quick_ideas: Keep every booking in one calendar with its status (enquiry, quoted, advance paid), so there's one truth
Confirm an event only after checking that calendar, so clashes are caught before they're promised.

workzap_build.text: an event booking calendar with status, venue and clash warnings, updated automatically as advances come in.

problems.free_stops: The booking statuses and confirmation flow are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many confirmed events already share the same date this month, so double-booking risk is seen before promises go out.
Give one person the job of writing every confirmed event in one dated notebook, so clashes are checked before saying yes.

problems.words: Quotes take me days to send and clients go elsewhere
quick_ideas: Keep your standard menus and per-head prices ready in one place, so quotes don't start from scratch
Reply to every enquiry the same day, even if only to say when the quote will come.

workzap_build.text: every enquiry recorded with a quick quote sent on WhatsApp and automatic follow-up reminders until it's booked or closed.

problems.ask_first: Where do most enquiries come from?
problems.free_stops: The quote builder and follow-up timing are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the time each enquiry arrived and when its quote was sent this week, so delay points in your quoting routine stand out.
Give one person a fixed daily time to send pending quotes from one running list, so fewer enquiries cool off.

problems.words: Plates, spoons and dishes go missing at every function
quick_ideas: Count crockery before and after the next event, so you know what actually goes missing
Give one person responsibility for crockery at each venue.

workzap_build.text: crockery and equipment check-out and check-in counts per event on phone, with a loss report every time.

problems.ask_first: What goes missing most — plates, cutlery or dishes?
problems.free_stops: The count routine and loss tracking per event stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the leaving count and return count of each crockery type after the next function, so the worst losses are clear.
Give one person one written return list for crockery at each event, so missing items are chased before everyone leaves.

problems.words: Balance payment after the wedding takes months, and advances are only in my diary
quick_ideas: List every unpaid balance with event date and amount, so you see who to chase
Give a written receipt for every advance, so there's a record on both sides.

workzap_build.text: advances and balances per event with automatic reminders before and after the event date.

problems.ask_first: How long do balances usually take?
problems.free_stops: The advance and balance terms and reminder schedule are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: List each completed event with whether any balance is still unpaid, so the oldest stuck money is obvious at once.
Give one person one notebook page for all advances and remaining balances, so follow-up no longer starts from scattered diary notes.

problems.words: Daily-wage waiters don't turn up on the night, and nobody knows who's in charge at the venue
quick_ideas: Confirm each waiter the day before the event, so no-shows are known in time to replace
Name one venue lead for every event, so the team and hall know who decides.

workzap_build.text: a staff roster per event with automatic WhatsApp confirmations the day before, and a run sheet shared with the venue lead.

problems.ask_first: How many waiters per event are daily-wage?
problems.free_stops: The roster and event-day run sheet are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count who was expected and who actually arrived at the next event, so the repeat no-shows become visible.
Give one person the venue lead job for each event and note it in one place, so staff know who decides on the night.

problems.words: Purchasing is done by one person and I don't trust the bills
quick_ideas: Ask for a photo of every bill on the day of purchase, so nothing is reconstructed later
Check one event's bills against market rates, so you know whether there's a real gap.

workzap_build.text: purchase requests and bill photos captured per event with your approval, totalled automatically against the event's budget.

problems.ask_first: Who buys for each event now?
problems.free_stops: The approval rules and bill-checking routine are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare purchase notes with the dishes actually served at one event, so billing gaps are easier to spot early.
Give one person the job of writing every purchase for an event in one notebook, so bill checking has a single trail.

problems.words: Wedding season we're overbooked, then months dead; leads from Instagram just ask the price and vanish
quick_ideas: Note which venues, planners and referrals brought past bookings, so you know where your business comes from
Approach offices for Ramadan iftar and corporate lunches, because they fill the off-season.

workzap_build.text: a lead source tracker showing which channel converts, plus a portfolio page with event photos and an enquiry form.

problems.ask_first: What do you do in the slow months now?
problems.free_stops: The off-season offer plan and lead tracking set-up stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which enquiries asked only for price and which became bookings this month, so the drop-off point is clearer.
Give one person one notebook list for venues and referral sources behind each booking, so off-season chasing follows what already works.

never_say: Anything on food-transport or holding rules, or event licensing — refer to the relevant authority.
Any interpretation of wedding-menu rules in Pakistan, or ways around them.
Help inflating bills to clients or creating fake receipts.
That an event will make a set profit or that headcount problems will stop.

sample_reply.person: Shaadi season mein guest zyada aa jate hain aur khana kam par jata hai. Is ka koi hal hai?
sample_reply.pi:
Ji, is ka rasta nikal sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, final headcount ki ek wazeh cut-off date client ko likh kar dein, taake aakhri waqt ki tabdeeli ka ek tay usool ho.
Doosra, extra mehmanon ka charge pehle se tay karein, kyunke event wali raat ye baat karna mushkil hota hai.
Lambay arse ke liye Workzap ye set kar sakta hai: har event ka headcount change log, client ko cut-off se pehle khud reminder, aur count ke hisaab se khareedari ki list update.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
